For the tool `actions_get`, which argument is described as: The unique identifier of the resource. This will vary based on the "method" provided, so ensure you provide the correct ID:
For the tool `actions_list`, which argument is described as: Filters for workflow jobs. **ONLY** used when method is 'list_workflow_jobs'
For the tool `actions_run_trigger`, which argument is described as: Inputs the workflow accepts. Only used for 'run_workflow' method.
For the tool `actions_run_trigger`, which argument is described as: The workflow ID (numeric) or workflow file name (e.g., main.yml, ci.yaml). Required for 'run_workflow' method.
For the tool `add_comment_to_pending_review`, which argument is described as: The side of the diff to comment on. LEFT indicates the previous state, RIGHT indicates the new state

For the tool `add_comment_to_pending_review`, which argument is described as: For multi-line comments, the starting side of the diff that the comment applies to. LEFT indicates the previous state, RIGHT indicates the new state

For the tool `add_issue_comment`, which argument is described as: The numeric ID of the issue or pull request comment to react to. Use this for reactions to comments; omit it to react to the issue or pull request itself. Cannot be combined with body.
For the tool `add_issue_comment`, which argument is described as: Emoji reaction to add. Required unless body is provided.
For the tool `add_issue_comment_reaction`, which argument is described as: The emoji reaction type
For the tool `add_pull_request_review_comment`, which argument is described as: The line number in the diff to comment on (optional)
For the tool `add_pull_request_review_comment`, which argument is described as: The side of the diff to comment on (optional)
For the tool `add_pull_request_review_comment`, which argument is described as: The start side of a multi-line comment (optional)

For the tool `add_pull_request_review_comment_reaction`, which argument is described as: The numeric pull request review comment ID. Use the number from a #discussion_r... anchor, not the GraphQL thread node ID (PRRT_...).

For the tool `add_reply_to_pull_request_comment`, which argument is described as: The numeric ID of the pull request review comment to reply or react to. Use the number from a #discussion_r... anchor, not the GraphQL thread node ID (PRRT_...).
For the tool `add_reply_to_pull_request_comment`, which argument is described as: Emoji reaction to add. Required unless body is provided.
For the tool `add_sub_issue`, which argument is described as: If true, reparent the sub-issue if it already has a parent

For the tool `assign_copilot_to_issue`, which argument is described as: Git reference (e.g., branch) that the agent will start its work from. If not specified, defaults to the repository's default branch

For the tool `assign_copilot_to_issue_with_intent`, which argument is described as: Git reference (e.g., branch) that the agent will start its work from. If not specified, defaults to the repository's default branch. Ignored when is_suggestion is true
For the tool `assign_copilot_to_issue_with_intent`, which argument is described as: Optional custom instructions to guide the agent beyond the issue body. Ignored when is_suggestion is true

For the tool `assign_copilot_to_issue_with_intent`, which argument is described as: One concise sentence explaining what specifically about the issue led to choosing Copilot. State the concrete signal (e.g. 'Well-scoped task with clear acceptance criteria').
For the tool `create_gist`, which argument is described as: Content for simple single-file gist creation
For the tool `create_gist`, which argument is described as: Filename for simple single-file gist creation
For the tool `create_issue`, which argument is described as: Issue number of the parent issue. The new issue is created and attached to this parent in the same operation.

For the tool `create_issue`, which argument is described as: Repository name of the parent issue. Must be provided with parent_owner. Omit both to use owner and repo. Only used when parent_issue_number is provided.
For the tool `create_or_update_file`, which argument is described as: Branch to create/update the file in
For the tool `create_pull_request`, which argument is described as: Allow maintainer edits
For the tool `create_pull_request_review`, which argument is described as: The SHA of the commit to review (optional, defaults to latest)
For the tool `create_pull_request_review`, which argument is described as: The pull request number
For the tool `create_repository`, which argument is described as: Repository description
For the tool `create_repository`, which argument is described as: Whether the repository should be private. Defaults to true (private) when omitted.
For the tool `create_repository_ruleset`, which argument is described as: Conditions for when this ruleset applies, e.g. {"ref_name": {"include": ["refs/heads/main"], "exclude": []}}
For the tool `create_repository_ruleset`, which argument is described as: Enterprise slug. Required when level is 'enterprise'.

For the tool `create_repository_ruleset`, which argument is described as: An array of rules within the ruleset. Each rule is an object with a 'type' (e.g. 'creation', 'deletion', 'non_fast_forward', 'required_signatures', 'pull_request', 'required_status_checks') and, for rules that need configuration, a 'parameters' object
For the tool `custom_properties_read`, which argument is described as: Enterprise slug. Required when level is 'enterprise'.
For the tool `custom_properties_write`, which argument is described as: Enterprise slug. Required when level is 'enterprise'.

For the tool `custom_properties_write`, which argument is described as: The custom properties to create or update. At the repository level each item assigns a value ('property_name' and 'value'); at the organization and enterprise levels each item defines the schema ('property_name' and 'value_type', plus optional definition fields).
For the tool `delete_pending_pull_request_review`, which argument is described as: The pull request number
For the tool `discussion_comment_write`, which argument is described as: Discussion number (required for 'add' and 'reply' methods)

For the tool `find_duplicate`, which argument is described as: Minimum similarity threshold a candidate must meet to be returned; higher values are stricter. When omitted, the API's high-precision default is used. The scale is defined by the API, so no client-side bounds are enforced.
For the tool `fork_repository`, which argument is described as: Organization to fork to
For the tool `get_code_scanning_alert`, which argument is described as: The number of the alert.
For the tool `get_dependabot_alert`, which argument is described as: The number of the alert.
For the tool `get_file_blame`, which argument is described as: Optional 1-based ending line of the window of interest. Must be >= start_line when both are provided.
For the tool `get_global_security_advisory`, which argument is described as: GitHub Security Advisory ID (format: GHSA-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx).
For the tool `get_job_logs`, which argument is described as: The unique identifier of the workflow job (required for single job logs)
For the tool `get_job_logs`, which argument is described as: Workflow run ID (required when using failed_only)
For the tool `get_job_logs`, which argument is described as: When true, gets logs for all failed jobs in the workflow run specified by run_id. Requires run_id to be provided.
For the tool `get_release_by_tag`, which argument is described as: Tag name (e.g., 'v1.0.0')
For the tool `get_repository_tree`, which argument is described as: Setting this parameter to true returns the objects or subtrees referenced by the tree. Default is false
For the tool `get_secret_scanning_alert`, which argument is described as: The number of the alert.
For the tool `hide_issue_comment`, which argument is described as: The reason for hiding the comment
For the tool `hide_pull_request_review`, which argument is described as: The reason for hiding the comment
For the tool `hide_pull_request_review`, which argument is described as: The numeric ID of the pull request review

For the tool `hide_pull_request_review_comment`, which argument is described as: The numeric pull request review comment ID. Use the number from a #discussion_r... anchor, not the GraphQL thread node ID (PRRT_...).
For the tool `issue_dependency_write`, which argument is described as: The number of the subject issue
For the tool `issue_dependency_write`, which argument is described as: The owner of the related issue's repository. Defaults to 'owner' when omitted.
For the tool `issue_read`, which argument is described as: The number of the issue
For the tool `issue_write`, which argument is described as: Issue number that this issue is a duplicate of. Required when state_reason is 'duplicate'.
For the tool `issue_write`, which argument is described as: Issue number to update

For the tool `issue_write`, which argument is described as: Issue number of the parent issue. Only used when method is 'create' and cannot be combined with issue_fields. The new issue is created and attached to this parent in the same operation.

For the tool `issue_write`, which argument is described as: Repository name of the parent issue. Must be provided with parent_owner. Omit both to use owner and repo. Only used when method is 'create' and parent_issue_number is provided.
For the tool `label_write`, which argument is described as: Label color as 6-character hex code without '#' prefix (e.g., 'f29513'). Required for 'create', optional for 'update'.
For the tool `label_write`, which argument is described as: New name for the label (used only with 'update' method to rename)
For the tool `list_code_scanning_alerts`, which argument is described as: The name of the tool used for code scanning.
For the tool `list_commits`, which argument is described as: Only commits after this date will be returned (ISO 8601 format: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ or YYYY-MM-DD)
For the tool `list_dependabot_alerts`, which argument is described as: Filter dependabot alerts by severity
For the tool `list_discussions`, which argument is described as: Order discussions by field. If provided, the 'direction' also needs to be provided.
For the tool `list_global_security_advisories`, which argument is described as: Filter advisories by affected package or version (e.g. "package1,package2@1.0.0").
For the tool `list_global_security_advisories`, which argument is described as: Filter by package ecosystem.
For the tool `list_global_security_advisories`, which argument is described as: Whether to only return withdrawn advisories.
For the tool `list_global_security_advisories`, which argument is described as: Filter by publish date or date range (ISO 8601 date or range).

For the tool `list_issues`, which argument is described as: Filter by custom issue field values. Each entry takes a field_name and a value; the server looks up the field and coerces the value to its type (single-select option name, text, number, or YYYY-MM-DD date).
For the tool `list_issues`, which argument is described as: Filter by date (ISO 8601 timestamp)
For the tool `list_notifications`, which argument is described as: Only show notifications updated after the given time (ISO 8601 format)
For the tool `list_secret_scanning_alerts`, which argument is described as: Filter by resolution
For the tool `manage_notification_subscription`, which argument is described as: Action to perform: ignore, watch, or delete the notification subscription.
For the tool `manage_repository_notification_subscription`, which argument is described as: Action to perform: ignore, watch, or delete the repository notification subscription.
For the tool `merge_pull_request`, which argument is described as: Extra detail for merge commit
For the tool `merge_pull_request`, which argument is described as: The expected SHA of the pull request's HEAD ref

For the tool `projects_get`, which argument is described as: Specific list of field names to include in the response when getting a project item (e.g. ["Status", "Priority"]). Resolved server-side to field IDs — pass this instead of 'fields' when you only know the human-readable names. Mutually exclusive with 'fields' — provide one, not both. Only used for 'get_project_item' method.
For the tool `projects_get`, which argument is described as: Owner type (user or org). If not provided, will be automatically detected.
For the tool `projects_get`, which argument is described as: The node ID of the project status update. Required for 'get_project_status_update' method.

For the tool `projects_list`, which argument is described as: Field names to include when listing project items (e.g. ["Status", "Priority"]). Resolved server-side to field IDs — pass this instead of 'fields' when you only know the human-readable names. Names that fail to resolve return a structured error. Mutually exclusive with 'fields' — provide one, not both. Only used for 'list_project_items' method.

For the tool `projects_list`, which argument is described as: The project's number. Required for 'list_project_fields', 'list_project_items', 'list_project_views', and 'list_project_status_updates' methods.
For the tool `projects_write`, which argument is described as: Saved view filter; omit on update to preserve it, or pass null to clear it.

For the tool `projects_write`, which argument is described as: The project item ID. Required for 'delete_project_item'. For 'update_project_item', provide either item_id, or (item_owner + item_repo + issue_number) to resolve the item by issue.

For the tool `projects_write`, which argument is described as: The name of the repository containing the issue or pull request. Required for 'add_project_item' method. Also accepted by 'update_project_item' when resolving the item by issue number.

For the tool `projects_write`, which argument is described as: The items to update with the top-level 'updated_field'. Required for 'update_project_items'; prefer it over calling 'update_project_item' in a loop. Each entry must match exactly one reference variant: 'node_id', numeric 'item_id', or 'item_owner' + 'item_repo' + 'issue_number'. Limit: 50 items per call.

For the tool `projects_write`, which argument is described as: Custom iterations for 'create_iteration_field' method. Only set this when you need iterations with varying durations, breaks between them, or specific titles. Otherwise omit it: GitHub auto-creates three iterations of 'iteration_duration' days starting on 'start_date', which is the right choice for most cases.
For the tool `projects_write`, which argument is described as: Owner type (user or org). Required for 'create_project' method. If not provided for other methods, will be automatically detected.

For the tool `projects_write`, which argument is described as: The pull request number (use when item_type is 'pull_request' for 'add_project_item' method). Provide either issue_number or pull_request_number.
For the tool `projects_write`, which argument is described as: The status of the project. Used for 'create_project_status_update' method.

For the tool `projects_write`, which argument is described as: The field/value to apply, using {"id": 123, "value": ...} or {"name": "Status", "value": ...}; null clears the field. Required for 'update_project_item' and 'update_project_items', where one top-level field/value applies to every item in a batch. For 'update_project_item' SINGLE_SELECT fields, the name form accepts option names; the ID form expects an option ID.

For the tool `projects_write`, which argument is described as: Ordered project field names to show on create or replace on update; omit on update to preserve, or pass [] to reset. Mutually exclusive with visible_fields. Roadmap accepts only [].

For the tool `pull_request_review_write`, which argument is described as: The node ID of the review thread (e.g., PRRT_kwDOxxx). Required for resolve_thread and unresolve_thread methods. Get thread IDs from pull_request_read with method get_review_comments.
For the tool `remove_issue_comment_reaction`, which argument is described as: The issue or pull request comment ID
For the tool `remove_issue_reaction`, which argument is described as: The reaction ID to remove
For the tool `remove_pull_request_review_comment_reaction`, which argument is described as: The reaction ID to remove
For the tool `remove_sub_issue`, which argument is described as: The ID of the sub-issue to remove. ID is not the same as issue number
For the tool `repository_ruleset_read`, which argument is described as: Branch name. Required for the 'get_rules_for_branch' method.
For the tool `repository_ruleset_read`, which argument is described as: Filter rule suites by ruleset evaluation mode. Used by the 'list_rule_suites' method.
For the tool `repository_ruleset_read`, which argument is described as: The level at which the ruleset is configured:
For the tool `repository_ruleset_read`, which argument is described as: Rule suite ID. Required for the 'get_rule_suite' method.
For the tool `repository_ruleset_read`, which argument is described as: Ruleset ID. Required for the 'get' method.
For the tool `reprioritize_sub_issue`, which argument is described as: The ID of the sub-issue to place this after (either after_id OR before_id should be specified)
For the tool `reprioritize_sub_issue`, which argument is described as: The parent issue number
For the tool `request_pull_request_reviewers`, which argument is described as: The pull request number
For the tool `resolve_review_thread`, which argument is described as: The node ID of the review thread to resolve (e.g., PRRT_kwDOxxx)
For the tool `set_issue_fields`, which argument is described as: The issue number to update
For the tool `sub_issue_write`, which argument is described as: The ID of the sub-issue to be prioritized before (either after_id OR before_id should be specified)
For the tool `sub_issue_write`, which argument is described as: When true, replaces the sub-issue's current parent issue. Use with 'add' method only.
For the tool `submit_pending_pull_request_review`, which argument is described as: The review action to perform
For the tool `unhide_issue_comment`, which argument is described as: The numeric ID of the issue or pull request conversation comment
For the tool `unhide_pull_request_review`, which argument is described as: The numeric ID of the pull request review
For the tool `unresolve_review_thread`, which argument is described as: The node ID of the review thread to unresolve (e.g., PRRT_kwDOxxx)
For the tool `update_gist`, which argument is described as: Updated description of the gist
For the tool `update_gist`, which argument is described as: ID of the gist to update
For the tool `update_issue_assignees`, which argument is described as: The issue number to update
For the tool `update_issue_comment`, which argument is described as: The numeric ID of the issue or pull request conversation comment to update. Do not use a pull request review comment ID.
For the tool `update_issue_labels`, which argument is described as: Labels to apply to this issue.
For the tool `update_issue_milestone`, which argument is described as: The milestone number to set on the issue

For the tool `update_issue_state`, which argument is described as: The issue number of the canonical issue this issue duplicates. Only valid when state_reason is 'duplicate'. Required when is_suggestion is true and state_reason is 'duplicate'. The issue number is resolved to a database ID before being sent to the API.
For the tool `update_issue_state`, which argument is described as: The issue number to update
For the tool `update_issue_state`, which argument is described as: The reason for the state change (only for closed state)

For the tool `update_issue_type`, which argument is described as: How confident you are in this choice. Use 'HIGH' for clear signal or explicit user request, 'MEDIUM' for reasonable inference with some ambiguity, 'LOW' for best guess with limited signal.
For the tool `update_issue_type`, which argument is described as: The issue number to update

For the tool `update_issue_type`, which argument is described as: One concise sentence explaining what specifically about the issue led you to choose this type. State the concrete signal (e.g. 'Reports a crash when saving' → bug, 'Asks for dark mode support' → feature).
For the tool `update_pull_request`, which argument is described as: Allow maintainer edits
For the tool `update_pull_request`, which argument is described as: GitHub usernames or ORG/team-slug team reviewers to request reviews from
For the tool `update_pull_request_branch`, which argument is described as: The expected SHA of the pull request's HEAD ref
For the tool `update_pull_request_draft_state`, which argument is described as: The pull request number
For the tool `update_pull_request_title`, which argument is described as: The pull request number
